findings.title: Removed .title float causes layout regression
findings.body: The `.title { float: left; }` rule inside `.contents` was deleted and not replaced by any flex-related ordering/positioning for `.title`. Since `.panel` now uses `@include order(3)` and `margin-left: auto` within a flex container, but `.title` and other direct children have no explicit `order`, the relative ordering/layout of title vs panel/icons is unspecified and likely breaks the previous visual layout (title no longer floats, and no flex item properties are set for it).

findings.title: Removed bullet margin-top regression
findings.body: The `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule was removed from `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` without replacement. This was presumably compensating for vertical alignment of the bullet badge; removing it may cause misalignment in the topic header area, especially since `.extra-info-wrapper` is now also assigned `@include order(2)` implying it participates in a flex layout where vertical centering may differ from before.

findings.title: .small-action-desc padding/margin changes not justified by flexbox need
findings.body: `.small-action-desc` padding was changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, `margin-top: 5px` was dropped, and `> p { padding-top: 4px; }` was removed. These are unrelated to the stated purpose of 'optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins' and change visual spacing in small-action messages (used for topic status changes), likely causing a regression in that area with no clear flex-related reasoning tying these changes together, and no test or visual verification is referenced.

findings.title: Switching plain CSS flex properties to vendor-prefixed mixins has no functional benefit here
findings.body: `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline;` were replaced with `@include inline-flex(); @include align-items(baseline);`, adding vendor prefixes for very old browsers (e.g., `-moz-inline-box`, `-ms-inline-flexbox`) that are no longer relevant for modern browser support. This increases CSS output size without any stated benefit, and conflicts with the PR's framing as a 'performance optimization' since it actually increases the compiled CSS payload.
